title: Stop losing permission dialogs raised while the transcript is open
description: Dialogs are delivered through a transient channel with no replay. The main prompt screen subscribes to it; the Ctrl+O transcript screen does not. A permission request raised while the transcript is open therefore finds no subscriber and is cancelled outright — the tool stays at "Waiting…" even after returning. This keeps pending requests and replays them to the next screen that subscribes.

sites.description:
The dialog channel factory: a zero-argument function returning an object with subscribe/reply/request that mints `dialog-<n>` ids. A second Map is declared alongside the existing pending map to hold the events themselves — the existing one stores resolvers, which cannot be replayed.

The pending map is read out of the first declaration by position, but the position is also asserted in `where`: if upstream reorders those bindings the site stops matching rather than capturing the wrong name, which is the failure mode worth having.

`if(<signal>?.aborted || <subscriberCount>===0)` cancels the request when nothing is listening. An aborted signal is a real cancellation and stays; having no subscriber right now is not, and is what this patch exists to stop. The test is narrowed to its left operand — captured as source, since it is an expression rather than a name.
The emit that publishes the request. Its argument is stored on the way past — `map.set(k,v)` returns the map, so `.get(k)` hands the same object straight on to emit without changing what is emitted.

Replay whatever is still pending to a newly-arrived listener. Guarded on the original map so anything already replied to or aborted is skipped, and deferred through queueMicrotask so the subscriber finishes wiring itself up first — the same ordering the channel already relies on for its cancellation path.
Drop the remembered event once answered, so a later subscriber is not shown a dialog that has already been dealt with.
